pokemon.name: Charizard
pokemon.strengths: High Special Attack and Speed. Excellent offensive coverage with Fire/Flying STAB.
pokemon.strategy: Charizard excels as a special attacker. Its 4× Rock weakness makes Stealth Rock devastating — always pair with a Rapid Spin or Defog user. Solar Power + Sun teams maximize its damage output.

pokemon.name: Blastoise
pokemon.strengths: Solid bulk on both sides. Access to Rapid Spin for hazard removal.
pokemon.strategy: Blastoise works best as a bulky spinner or special tank. Rain Dish + Rain teams give it passive recovery. Mega Blastoise with Mega Launcher boosts Pulse moves significantly.

pokemon.name: Venusaur
pokemon.strengths: Great bulk and Chlorophyll doubles Speed in sun. Grass/Poison gives good defensive typing.
pokemon.strategy: Venusaur shines on Sun teams with Chlorophyll. Sleep Powder + Growth makes it a dangerous sweeper. Also effective as a bulky pivot with Giga Drain recovery.

pokemon.name: Pikachu
pokemon.strengths: Light Ball doubles Attack and Special Attack. Fast but fragile.
pokemon.strategy: Pikachu is only viable with Light Ball. Volt Tackle hits hard but has recoil. In competitive, outclassed by Raichu and other Electric types, but Light Ball makes it a glass cannon.

pokemon.name: Garchomp
pokemon.strengths: Incredible Attack and Speed. Dragon/Ground STAB covers most of the metagame.
pokemon.strategy: Garchomp is one of the most dominant Pokemon in competitive play. Swords Dance + Scale Shot makes it a terrifying sweeper. Its 4× Ice weakness is the main vulnerability — always scout for Ice Beam/Ice Shard.

pokemon.name: Dragonite
pokemon.strengths: Multiscale halves damage at full HP. Extreme Speed provides priority. Versatile attacker.
pokemon.strategy: Multiscale + Dragon Dance is Dragonite's bread and butter. Set up on a resisted hit, then sweep. Extreme Speed picks off weakened threats. Keep Stealth Rock off the field to preserve Multiscale.

pokemon.name: Tyranitar
pokemon.strengths: Sand Stream boosts SpDef by 50%. Massive Attack and good bulk. Excellent trapper with Pursuit.
pokemon.strategy: Tyranitar's Sand Stream makes it a premier weather setter. Its 4× Fighting weakness is brutal, but its SpDef in sand is enormous. Use as a Stealth Rock setter, Pursuit trapper, or Dragon Dance sweeper.

pokemon.name: Lucario
pokemon.strengths: Excellent offensive typing. Can go physical or special. Many resistances from Steel type.
pokemon.strategy: Lucario is a versatile sweeper that can run physical (Swords Dance) or special (Nasty Plot) sets. Its Steel typing gives 9 resistances. Mega Lucario with Adaptability is devastating — Close Combat hits like a truck.

pokemon.name: Gengar
pokemon.strengths: Blazing Speed and Special Attack. Three immunities (Normal, Fighting, Ground with Levitate in older gens).
pokemon.strategy: Gengar is a classic special sweeper and spinblocker. Nasty Plot + 3 attacks is devastating. In modern gens without Levitate, Ground coverage is a real threat. Use its immunities to switch in safely.

pokemon.name: Scizor
pokemon.strengths: Technician Bullet Punch is one of the best priority moves. Only one weakness (Fire). Excellent pivot with U-turn.
pokemon.strategy: Scizor's only weakness is a 4× Fire weakness, but everything else it handles well. Technician Bullet Punch picks off faster threats. Choice Band U-turn generates momentum. Swords Dance sets can sweep late-game.

pokemon.name: Gyarados
pokemon.strengths: Intimidate lowers opponent's Attack on switch-in. Dragon Dance sweeper. Moxie snowballs KOs.
pokemon.strategy: Gyarados is a top-tier Dragon Dance sweeper. Intimidate gives it setup opportunities. Its 4× Electric weakness means one Thunderbolt ends it — never stay in on Electric types. Moxie variant snowballs after the first KO.

pokemon.name: Swampert
pokemon.strengths: Only one weakness (Grass, 4×). Electric immunity. Great bulk and offensive presence.
pokemon.strategy: Water/Ground is one of the best defensive typings — only weak to Grass. Swampert sets Stealth Rock reliably and hits hard. Mega Swampert with Swift Swim in rain is a terrifying sweeper with boosted Speed.

pokemon.name: Metagross
pokemon.strengths: Incredible Attack and Defense. Steel/Psychic gives many resistances. Clear Body prevents stat drops.
pokemon.strategy: Metagross is a physical powerhouse with excellent bulk. Meteor Mash + Attack boost chance is deadly. Mega Metagross with Tough Claws is one of the strongest Mega Evolutions. Use Bullet Punch for priority.

pokemon.name: Salamence
pokemon.strengths: Intimidate + Dragon Dance. Can go physical or mixed. Moxie for snowballing.
pokemon.strategy: Salamence is a fearsome Dragon Dance sweeper. Intimidate gives it setup turns. Like Dragonite, 4× Ice weakness is the Achilles heel. Mega Salamence with Aerilate turns Return into a 120 BP Flying STAB.

pokemon.name: Togekiss
pokemon.strengths: Serene Grace + Air Slash = 60% flinch chance. Great special bulk. Dragon immunity.
pokemon.strategy: Togekiss is the king of flinch hax. Thunder Wave + Air Slash with Serene Grace is infuriating to face. Fairy/Flying gives Dragon immunity and Fighting resistance. Use Roost to stay healthy.

pokemon.name: Ferrothorn
pokemon.strengths: Incredible physical and special bulk. Iron Barbs punishes contact moves. Hazard setter.
pokemon.strategy: Ferrothorn is one of the best defensive Pokemon ever. 4× Fire weakness is its only real flaw. Stealth Rock + Leech Seed + Iron Barbs chips everything. Gyro Ball hits hard due to its abysmal Speed.

pokemon.name: Corviknight
pokemon.strengths: Mirror Armor reflects stat drops. Excellent defensive typing. Reliable Defog user.
pokemon.strategy: Corviknight is a premier physical wall and Defog user. Mirror Armor punishes Intimidate and Sticky Web. Flying/Steel gives many resistances and a Ground immunity. Roost keeps it healthy throughout the match.

pokemon.name: Dragapult
pokemon.strengths: Blazing 142 base Speed. Versatile — physical, special, or support sets. Two immunities.
pokemon.strategy: Dragapult's Speed tier is nearly unmatched. It can run physical (Dragon Darts), special (Shadow Ball + Draco Meteor), or even support (Will-O-Wisp + Hex). Its unpredictability is its greatest weapon.

pokemon.name: Blaziken
pokemon.strengths: Speed Boost makes it faster every turn. Devastating Attack with Fire/Fighting STAB.
pokemon.strategy: Speed Boost Blaziken is banned to Ubers for good reason. Protect + Speed Boost + Swords Dance = unstoppable. Flare Blitz and Close Combat hit incredibly hard. Its frailty means it can't take many hits though.

pokemon.name: Gardevoir
pokemon.strengths: Excellent Special Attack and SpDef. Psychic/Fairy is great offensive typing. Trace copies abilities.
pokemon.strategy: Gardevoir is a potent special attacker with Calm Mind. Psychic/Fairy STAB hits Fighting, Dragon, and Poison types. Mega Gardevoir with Pixilate turns Hyper Voice into a spread Fairy move. Trace can steal key abilities.

pokemon.name: Infernape
pokemon.strengths: Great Speed and mixed offenses. Iron Fist boosts punch moves. Versatile attacker.
pokemon.strategy: Infernape is the most versatile Fire/Fighting starter. It can go physical, special, or mixed. Iron Fist + Mach Punch gives it priority. U-turn generates momentum. Faster and more flexible than Blaziken without Speed Boost.

pokemon.name: Magearna
pokemon.strengths: Steel/Fairy is the best defensive typing in the game. Soul-Heart boosts SpAtk on KOs. Incredible bulk.
pokemon.strategy: Magearna has the best typing in Pokemon — Steel/Fairy resists 9 types and is immune to Dragon. Soul-Heart snowballs Special Attack. Fleur Cannon hits hard but drops SpAtk, so Volt Switch out after. Trick Room sets are also effective.

pokemon.name: Landorus-Therian
pokemon.strengths: Intimidate + U-turn = best pivot in the game. Electric immunity. Stealth Rock setter.
pokemon.strategy: Landorus-T is arguably the most used Pokemon in competitive history. Intimidate + U-turn cycle is unmatched for momentum. Sets Stealth Rock reliably. 4× Ice weakness is exploitable but its utility is irreplaceable.

pokemon.name: Mimikyu
pokemon.strengths: Disguise guarantees a free turn. Ghost/Fairy is excellent offensive typing. Shadow Sneak priority.
pokemon.strategy: Mimikyu's Disguise ability is essentially a free Swords Dance. Ghost/Fairy STAB hits almost everything neutrally. Shadow Sneak provides priority after setup. One of the best sweepers in the game thanks to its guaranteed setup turn.

pokemon.name: Toxapex
pokemon.strengths: Absurd physical and special bulk. Regenerator heals on switch. Scald burns physical attackers.
pokemon.strategy: Toxapex is the ultimate wall. 152 Defense and 142 SpDef with Regenerator makes it nearly unkillable. Scald's 30% burn chance cripples physical attackers. Toxic Spikes + Haze shuts down setup sweepers.
